messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a cluster-wide spike in GPU attach latency in eu-west3 coinciding with nightly ephemeral NVMe scrubs. Batch pools blocked during the 02:00 scrub window. Logs + quick snapshot below.

jon: saw it too, attach p95 went from ~20s to ~110s around 02:10.

lee: iostat on scratch devices shows sustained 99% util and long await. snippet:
```
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
sda             6.5  134.2  1024k  81920  608.0   48.2   18.2   1.2  99.7
```

sarah: looks like scrub concurrency is overlapping with batch attach window. we pushed the scrub change last week for faster reclamation.

frank: if we lower scrub concurrency we'll reduce io pressure but increase backlog / wear exposure. cost tradeoff: more sustained writes later vs immediate attach failures.

maria: proposal: canary change in eu-west3 on 50 nodes -> reduce scrub concurrency 8->3, and temporarily raise ioquota for batch-pool (allow higher burst) for next 6 hours. rollout plan below.

jon: +1 for canary. also add a short-term throttle on janitor delete workers to avoid overlapping small writes.

k8s-bot: Warning — 12 pending gpu-attach events in batch-pool-eu-west3; avg pending time 74s.

ops-bot: Alert suppressed for 30m while mitigation in progress (runbook: /runbooks/ephemeral-io).

lee: ran a quick sim on 10 nodes: reduced concurrency -> iostat %util dropped to 65% and attach p95 improved to 28s.

frank: can we schedule permanent change to scrub cadence (move to 03:30) instead of always delaying later? that keeps night traffic lower for batch windows. need to model backlog growth.

maria: action items: 1) frank to run scrub-backlog forecast (ETA 3h), 2) jon to start canary change now on 50 nodes and report attach p95 every 10m, 3) lee to patch janitor throttle for batch-pools, 4) sarah to open infra-cost thread comparing reserved IO bursts vs capacity planning.

jon: starting canary now — kicking off playbook: `scripts/scrub-tune --cluster eu-west3 --nodes 50 --concurrency 3`

maria: thanks — label this P2 for visibility. if canary looks good we'll roll to the rest of eu-west3 and consider a global schedule change.

sarah: noted, will draft cost analysis and link it here.

ops-bot: Canary finished step 1: config applied to 50 nodes. Monitoring for 30m.

maria: ping if you see any regression, otherwise we'll reconvene in 45m to decide full rollout. :coffee:
